(manifest row 243, Round 11 / P34, sub-round 11A) · **Base:**
`r11/P34.34b-export-mode-ci-build-and-island-budgets` · **Gate:** none ·

## Why

A research-dossier page could present a stand-in as a capture (the fixture
assertions carried retrieval-shaped stamps) and an unreviewed dossier as
reviewed (the page hard-coded "Reviewed research dossier" over a packet whose
`review.status` is `not_run`). C4 found NEW-2, NEW-3, NEW-22, NEW-23 and
NEW-32; F-16 challenges the Round-10 dossier verdicts that rested on
unlabelled stand-ins. This row makes the rendered surface say, for every
assertion, how its bytes were obtained — and makes the non-live posture
visible above the fold — while the route stays internal.

## What ships

- **Acquisition vocabulary + labels** (`exports/src/exports/research_dossier.py`):
  `live_capture` / `committed_transcription` / `stand_in` derived from the
  evidence record (`capture_kind`, `access_mode`, `capture_method`,
  `extraction_method`, `retrieved_date`) — never inferred from a URL.
  Fail-closed: no retrieval stamp and no live marker derives `stand_in`.
  Every assertion and ledger row carries `acquisition`; the dossier carries
  `evidence_posture` (counts + which facts rest on stand-ins — the F-16
  disclosure half).
- **Review label from the record:** `review_label()` maps the recorded
  `review_status` (`completed` → "independently reviewed", `pending` →
  "independent review pending", `not_run` → "independent review not yet run").
  Nothing renders "reviewed" for `not_run` — page, print or JSON.
- **True dates + the build-clock guard** (DR-C4-15): the packet validator and
  `build_dossier` reject displayed stamps later than the build clock;
  `displayed_date_violations` walks the composed render; `data.ts` runs
  `assertNoFutureDisplayDates` on every portfolio load so the web build
  fails the same way. Stated document dates (`valid_from`/`valid_to`) are
  real-world claims, exempt by design.
- **Licence, permalink, per-page as-of** (SIG-LIC-011, C4 NEW-22/23): the
  dossier JSON carries `licence` (artifact + per-record spdx), `permalink`
  (`https://surveillancegraph.org/research-dossier/<slug>/`) and `as_of`;
  the print footer repeats all three on every printed page; the page
  renders the same line.
- **Web mirror** (`web/src/lib/research-dossier.ts` + pages): the same
  vocabulary, `acquisitionLabel`/`derivedAcquisition`/`evidencePosture`/
  `reviewLabel`/`dossierLicenceText`/`dossierPermalink` helpers; the
  `[slug]` page gains an "obtained" column on every assertion row and the
  ledger, the above-the-fold non-live disclosure (counts by class), the
  record-derived review wording, and the licence/permalink/as-of line; the
  index labels each dossier's review state from its record.
- **Regenerated artifact sets** — the three dossier runs re-emitted into
  `docs/build/reports/p32.1{8,9}-*-dossier_2026-10-07/` and
  `p32.20-san-diego-dossier_2026-10-07/` with `SUPERSEDES.json` digests of
  both sets; each original `CORRECTION.md` gained the append-only
  successor pointer (ADR-146 D2: superseded bytes untouched).
- **Copy-batch record:** the four new page sentences are pending rows
  RD-01…RD-04 in `docs/build/reports/copy-batches/batch-02.md` — they ship
  only after the operator's verbatim confirmation (B-2); bound elements
  carry `data-copy`.
